source_first_claims.claim: Visual singleton search operationally uses exogenous attentional allocation; top-down selective factors must be controlled.
V1 hypothesis: local salience equals relative maximum V1 neural population response at each location, regardless of the winning neuron feature tuning.
Iso-feature contextual suppression releases response of appropriately tuned neurons at singleton compared with identically featured background bars.
The target is a parameter-free distributional behavioral test, NOT fully parameterized V1 network simulation or neuronal recording.
For fixed background other-item response distribution, higher maximum V1 target response yields monotonically shorter salience-driven singleton-search RT under fixed motor/readout mapping.
Each singleton’s response distribution is treated as statistically independent of the fixed non-target background and appropriate other feature fluctuations.
For C/O/CO example, absence of CO jointly tuned neuron yields response-to-RT minimum-race equality, motivating model controls.
Feature-specific V1 neural response maxima distinguish alternative color-tuned, orientation-tuned and joint-tuned cell contributions.
Source expands conditions to seven singleton categories C,M,O,CM,CO,MO,CMO on matched homogeneous color/motion/orientation backgrounds.
The derivation uses RT induced by a monotone transform of maximum evoked V1 population responses, and race minima correspond to maximum of response collections.
Jointly feature-tuned CO and MO cells yield expected violations of some simple double- and triple-feature spurious race equalities.
CM jointly tuned cell prevalence and response strength is uncertain in original source, making relevant spurious equality ambiguous.
Original central non-spurious race equality: min(RT_CMO, RT_C, RT_M, RT_O) =d min(RT_CM, RT_CO, RT_MO) assuming no V1 CMO-tuned cells.

source_first_claims.original_source_locator: p16 Eq30 and p32–34 Methods Eq39
source_first_claims.claim: Eq30 is derived via identical maxima over six classes of V1 neurons C/M/O/CM/CO/MO on both sides of the response-to-RT mapping.
The CMO RT distribution is indirectly predicted by distributional data from six other singleton conditions of the SAME observer, no fitted free prediction parameters.
The source Fig6 shows example observer SA p=.094; Fig7 shows all six observers’ Eq30 predictions non-rejected at p>.05, NOT independently reproduced statistics.
Matched-complexity spurious control equalities RE6 and RE7 are falsified for illustrated subject SA, whereas RE8 is not.
Source reports 80 or 320 analysis configurations across bin counts, bin definitions and discrepancy metrics; RE1 robustness limited by empirical statistical power.
In green vs purple trials rapid color pop-out creates potential latency floor and weaker rejection of some spurious controls.
Previously collected Koene/Zhaoping 2007 RT data used: 30x22 bar grid; 18 possible target cells, left/right manual press, seven singleton categories.
About 300 RT per singleton type per observer split into green/purple pools averaging ~150 each; eight original observers but only six recorded CMO.
Excluded incorrect presses, RT<.2s and subject/category RT>3 SD; reused stimulus/calibration means findings are task-conditioned.
Non-spurious Eq30 proof hinges on feature-matched distribution invariances and max/min race identity; not proof across alternative sensorimotor distributions.
Original conditional interpretation suggests extrastriate weak salience contribution for these singleton scenes only if extrastriate triple-tuned responses materially break Eq30.
Original explicit alternative: extrastriate CMO responses can be negligible or satisfy Eq35, preserving behavioral Eq30 even with extrastriate participation.
Original authors flag independent fluctuations, fixed background, non-tuned-feature invariance, contrast normalization, imperfect isoluminance and stable perceptual learning as idealizations.
Complex images, multiple eye movements, goal-driven predictable feature attention violate simple RT monotonicity; no full cognitive generative model identified.
The V1 race model descends from early Li/Zhaoping V1 saliency work and reutilizes original Koene/Zhaoping 2007 behavioral trial data, not wholly novel invented mechanism.

per_claim_original_source_reread.review: Original pp4–6 requires clean exogenous context; stop strong generality.

Confirmed p4–7 iso-feature suppression source key.
Confirmed pp6–7 study is mathematical parameter-free inference over reused behavior; not new direct neuronal recording.
Confirmed pp7–8 Eq3–4 conditioned on same background distribution.
Challenge B01: original pp25–27 permits normalization/correlations and assumes independence approximations; narrow if stated universally.
Simple race equality source illustrates specific absent conjunctive neuron example; do not generalize as guaranteed across CO cells.
Confirmed source cell families p11 Fig4.
Confirmed p11 Fig4 seven feature categories.
Confirmed pp13–14 Eqs17–23 monotone f(max) with same background.
Original pp14–16 says expected likely inequality, not theorem with guaranteed CO/MO response amplitudes.
Confirmed pp15–16 and Discussion CM uncertainty.
Confirmed exact Eq30 p16 = distributional race equality; require no CMO and approximations.

Challenge B02: no free coefficients for derived relation means input histograms/optimization and metric/test parameters still exist; avoid entirely parameter-free experimental analysis.
Challenge B03: p>.05 six observers = nonrejection under bounded sensitivity; 'confirmed' author sense not mathematical unique correctness.
Confirmed Fig8 p20 two spurious rejected, RE8 remains.
Confirmed Table1 and Fig10 method-param counts conditional.
Original green floor weakening included.
Confirmed original Koene/Zhaoping 2007 trial reuse, pp28–30; no independently fresh 2015 cohort.
Confirm six CMO and eight singles/doubles, ~300 combined, ~150 per color pool.
Confirmed original exclusion filters (0.2 seconds, >3 SD).
Challenge B04: proof p32–34 also needs independence of noise and feature-distribution noninteraction; maximum-of-populations not direct synaptic circuit measurement.
Challenge B05: Discussion expressly cannot firmly establish zero extrastriate, also fast target possibility.
Confirmed Eq35 and negligibility escape.
Challenge B06: color isoluminance 'matched' not individualized; if A22 implies fully calibrated condition correct.
Confirmed complex scenes, top down limits p27.
Confirmed earlier V1 salience and dataset ancestry; additional lineage comparison P05 not to be turned into independence claim.

objections.source: original PDF p26 Discussion; pp32–34 Methods
objections.issue: A06 independence is paper assumption, no direct measured neuronal fluctuation independence; do not infer full neuronal generative identification.
objections.requested: Explicitly condition all race claims on neuron-pool response and background independence approximations.

objections.source: original PDF pp18–23 Fig8–10 Table1 and Methods Eq43–45
objections.issue: Parameter-free theoretical race identity still uses source-chosen histogram bins, discrepancy metrics and optimization to infer/test held-out RT_CMO.
objections.requested: Limit parameter-free to no tuned V1 prediction free coefficients given empirically measured six RT distributions; report test procedure has finite hyperparameters.

objections.source: original PDF p19 Fig7, p23 Fig10,p25 discussion
objections.issue: Six p>.05 source outcomes are nonrejections, neither direct neural proof nor general full-generative uniqueness.
objections.requested: Keep limited power and nonuniqueness; source numeric values not independently recomputed.

objections.source: original PDF p16 Eq30,p33 Methods Eq39
objections.issue: Eq30 printed as stochastic distribution relation for MIN races under f(max), not deterministic subject-independent equality of each observed trial RT.
objections.requested: Represent equality in distribution and conditional proof, not pathwise trial identity.

objections.source: original PDF pp26–28 extrastriate Discussion Eq35
objections.issue: Even if V1 suitable, extrastriate with invariant or negligible triple-tuned response could preserve race distribution.
Actual fixed luminance/saturation vs individual observer precise isoluminance calibration distinction can contaminate context assumptions.
objections.requested: A26 already states imperfect isoluminance; keep limitation, no duplicate patch.

objections.issue: Original source does not establish absence of all spurious race survival; RE8 often survives and CM remains uncertain.
objections.requested: Keep exact rejected vs non-rejected controls with conditional power.
